purpose: Permethrin is used to treat head lice and scabies, which are tiny bugs or mites that live on your skin or hair and cause itching. It kills the bugs and their eggs. It is applied directly to the skin or hair, not taken by mouth.
how_it_works: Permethrin works by attacking the nervous system of lice and mites, causing them to become paralyzed and die. Think of it like a poison that is specifically designed to affect insects and mites but is very safe for people when used as directed. It stays on the skin or hair for a little while to keep killing any bugs that may hatch after the first treatment.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are mild and happen right where you apply it — things like temporary burning, stinging, itching, tingling, redness, or a rash on the skin. These usually go away on their own. Some scalp numbness or mild swelling is also possible.
warnings: Do not use this near your eyes or inside your nose or mouth — rinse right away with water if it gets there. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or treating a baby under 2 months old before using it. Some people are allergic to chrysanthemums or ragweed and may be more likely to have a reaction. If itching or a rash gets much worse after using it, call your doctor.
typical_dosing: For head lice: Shampoo your hair first, then apply permethrin cream rinse to damp hair, leave it on for 10 minutes, then rinse off. A second treatment is usually done 9 to 10 days later. For scabies: Apply the cream from neck to toe at bedtime, leave it on for 8 to 14 hours, then wash it off. Your doctor may recommend a second treatment one week later.
